uuid@10.0.0 is vulnerable to CVE-2026-41907 (MEDIUM severity, silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers in v3/v5/v6 functions). The fix is available in uuid@11.1.1. However, upgrading from uuid@10.x to uuid@11.x is a major version jump that would require significant testing and may introduce breaking changes in transitive dependencies. The vulnerability affects applications that pass external buffers to uuid v3/v5/v6 functions with attacker-controlled offsets or undersized buffers; langfuse's typical usage does not expose this attack surface.

uuid@3.3.3 is vulnerable to CVE-2026-41907 (MEDIUM severity, silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers in v3/v5/v6 functions). The fix is available in uuid@11.1.1. However, upgrading from uuid@3.x to uuid@11.x crosses multiple major versions (the API and module layout changed substantially across v7/v9/v11) and would require significant testing and may introduce breaking changes in transitive dependencies that deep-import legacy uuid entry points. The vulnerability affects applications that pass external buffers to uuid v3/v5/v6 functions with attacker-controlled offsets or undersized buffers; langfuse's typical usage does not expose this attack surface.

Upgrading uuid from 3.x/9.x/10.x to the fixed version 11.1.1 requires a major version bump that cannot be applied safely and with confidence in OpenSearch Dashboards. Waiting for upstream to address compatibility issues.

CVE-2026-41907 is patched in uuid 11.1.1. Trigger.dev's lockfile still resolves uuid 3.x/8.x/9.x/10.x for legacy transitive consumers; forcing those majors to 11.x breaks API compatibility. The webapp's uuid@^11 consumers already receive 11.1.1+ via pnpm overrides. Assessing reachability and upstream migration for the remaining legacy uuid resolutions.

The missing buffer bounds check (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) only triggers when a caller passes an output buffer to uuid v3/v5/v6. Uptime Kuma generates random v4 UUIDs and does not invoke the v3/v5/v6 buffer APIs, so the vulnerable path is not exercised by the application. The first fixed release (11.1.1) is a major version bump from the 8.x/10.x copies still resolved transitively (via hyperid and dockerode), which carries breaking-change risk that is being evaluated. Reachability proof and a non-breaking remediation are under assessment.
